newsitem.title: zaire: Zaire says former premier Kengo fled to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says former premier Kengo fled to Europe.

text.p: Zaire is issuing an international warrant for the arrest of former prime minister Kengo wa Dondo who is in Europe, Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba said on Tuesday.
He said the new government team which took over after Kengo was sacked three weeks ago had found the national treasury empty.
"An international warrant is being issued for Kengo's arrest. At least he can tell us where all the money is gone," Kin-Kiey told a news conference.
State television said the government was also pursuing judicial proceedings against Kengo's economic team.

"We understand that serious accusations have been raised against the outgoing government's economic team. Judicial proceedings have been initiated against the said members," the television reported on its main evening news.
"At the moment the former prime minister has left the country," the television said.
Sources close to Kengo said he left Zaire on Sunday for Switzerland.
A government spokesman earlier said Kengo had not given a proper account of his government finances to his successor, General Likulia Bolongo, who took over last week.

Kengo was voted out of office about three weeks ago. A part Tutsi, he had been widely accused of weakness in the face of a rebellion launched from eastern Zaire last October, initially by ethnic Tutsis.
Rebels now hold about half the country and are advancing on the capital Kinshasa.

Zaire's economy has practically collapsed following decades of mismanagement and corruption and its treasury has been in the red for years. Kengo had been praised in the West for trying to reform the economy.
Since the start of the rebellion in eastern Zaire, the military high command and Kengo's government have traded accusations over the handling of war finances.
"It's a settling of scores. No one is cleaner than the other," said a close aide of the former prime minister, who asked not to be named.
